notes:
The 1886 report is divided into 38 consecutive sections covering lines 1-11361 with no gaps or overlaps; I read every line. Quotes are copied exactly but without the trailing space that ends every OCR line.

General points for the cutter:
(1) Page headers recur inside every section and should be stripped: 'nn REPORT ON THE MIGRATION OF BIRDS.' on even pages, '<COAST NAME>. nn' on odd ones. Page numbers are often garbled ('D2)', 'IES)', 'WBZ', 'Q1', 'OT', 'EZ', 'CL', 'AD5', '05', 'P53', 'ial'), and one header has no number at all (4723).
(2) Footnotes at the page foot start with '1', '*', '!', '3' or '~ 1' and interrupt the running text.
(3) Words hyphenated at line ends are split ('Gan- / nets').
(4) Where a page header comes just before a coast heading (543, 1883, 3320, 4573, 7193), I put the header in the new coast's section.
(5) Printed page 1 of the East Coast of Scotland was scanned twice (440-541, which duplicates 543-599). Skip the first copy.
(6) On neither Scottish coast is the 'Diary from the Stations' a by-date diary. Both are by station, with long letters. Their species parts are by FAMILY, not by species, and are the only place the Scottish schedules' records appear, so I marked them primary.
(7) The East Coast of England has no diary. Its species notes are the primary records and often run several species together in one paragraph, starting mid-line.
(8) The West Coast of England is the only true by-date diary (spring 4904-5122, autumn 5123-6316). Its species notes (6317-7003) are marked summary, but they also hold records the diary leaves out, so don't discard them blindly.
(9) Ireland's species notes are bird headings with station paragraphs under them.
(10) Small tables inside prose or species sections are flagged in the section notes rather than split off: Swallow arrivals 1292-1305, Curlew/Woodcock counts 1748-1773. The Solan Goose daily table (1551-1600) has its own section because it holds primary daily records.
(11) There are three tabulated specimen lists whose entries also appear in the species notes: E. England wings 3119-3170, Irish legs and wings 7630-8254, and (as prose) the Irish introduction.
(12) The contents list (181-193) and the stations' own lists name the Irish part 'IRISH Coasts' / 'IRISH COAST'; I used the running heading 'IRISH COAST'. The West England coast name is given as its heading prints, 'WEST COAST OF ENGLAND AND WALES, AND THE ISLE OF MAN'; its page headers omit 'THE'.</notes>
